newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse stops Marsteel price rise.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse stops Marsteel price rise.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) stopped on Tuesday a surge in the share price of holding firm Marsteel Consolidated Inc.
The stock exchange froze the price of Marsteel A and B shares after they both reached four centavos, showing a 48.15 percent hike from 2.7 centavos on Monday.
The PSE surveillance department said there had been no disclosure that could have affected the firm's share.
In late session, a total of 14.2 million Marsteel A shares and 90.30 million B shares were traded.
Under bourse rules, any further rise in a share price is frozen if it rises by close to 50 percent in a session. The issue can then be traded only at or below the price at which it was frozen.
"There's unconfirmed talk of backdoor listing involving the company," said Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital Equities.
Marsteel officials were not immediately available for comment.
